title: Replace the dusty filter under a machine's spring-shut intake cover with the new filter
instruction: Replace the grey dusty filter in the machine's air intake with the new white filter, putting the old one in the bin. Leave the cover shut and take both arms back to where they started.
context: Air-intake filters on machines, appliances and air purifiers sit behind sprung covers that snap shut when let go, so changing one means keeping the cover open while the dusty filter comes out and the new one goes in.
setup: A table in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Distances are measured forward from the line between the arm bases and sideways from the midpoint between them. (1) A machine's air intake, fixed: a light grey 1 mm sheet-steel housing 24 cm deep (18 to 42 cm forward), 23.5 cm across (from 21 cm right to 2.5 cm left of the centre line) and 10 cm tall, with a grille on its front. In its top, an opening 20 x 12 cm (20 to 40 cm forward, 7 to 19 cm right of the centre line) over the filter slot, whose floor is 1.5 cm above the table: the filter stands upright across the slot, held at its two ends by dark steel rail channels (each a 2.4 cm wide channel between 6 mm plates 1.6 cm long, closed by a 6 mm end plate, 3.5 cm tall), so the filter has 6 mm of play either side. (2) A grey ABS cover 2 mm thick (modelled 6 mm), 120 g, over the top, hinged along the housing's left top edge and held shut by a torsion spring of 0.003 N m per degree (0.21 N m at 70 degrees open, about 2.3 N on the pedal); its tail sticks out 9 cm past the hinge to the left, rising 15 degrees, with a black rubber pedal (5 x 3.5 cm) on its end. Pressing the pedal down swings the cover up (about 70 degrees with the pedal near the table, 88 at most); let go, it shuts. (3) The old filter, grey with dust, 60 g: pleated polyester media in a card frame, 11 cm long, 1.2 cm thick and 3.5 cm tall, with a black ABS tab 3 x 1.2 x 3.5 cm on top, standing in the slot along the forward line, 30 cm forward and 13 cm right of the centre line, its tab's top 1.5 cm below the housing's top. (4) A new filter, the same but white, standing in a grey ABS holder (a base 15 x 5 x 1 cm with the same rail channels, 3 cm tall) 37 cm forward and 26 cm right of the centre line. (5) A blue plastic bin (13 x 10 cm inside, 7 cm tall) 20 cm forward and 27 cm right of the centre line. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Judged at the end of the trial. 1.0: the new filter seated in the slot (its underside within 1 cm of the slot's floor, upright within 12 degrees), the old one in the bin, the cover shut (within 5 degrees) and both hands let go (each gripper's fingertip centre, TCP, at least 4 cm from the pedal and from both filters' tabs) and both arms back where they started (each TCP within 5 cm of its start); 0.5: the new filter seated and the old one in the bin, otherwise; 0.25: the old filter in the bin; else 0.0. The trial ends at the run limit, or once the full score has held for 1 s with the cover and both filters still.
reset_notes: Put the grey filter back in the slot and the white one back in its holder; the cover shuts by itself.
fidelity: Rigid-body PhysX (Isaac Sim 6.1, 20 Hz control) at real size and mass. Simplified: the cover is one rigid plate with its pedal tail on a hinge whose spring stands in for the torsion spring (0.003 N m per degree); the filters are rigid panels (no pleats to flex, no dust); the housing is fixed. Cameras 1280 x 704 (Dream-1 sees 320 x 176).
